LineageOS comes from the hallowed lineage of Cyanogenmod, one of the most-popular early alternate firmware projects for Android-compatible phones.

1st generation Google Pixel happily chugging along on LineageOS over here (though getting Google's voice-control to work and stay working on it can be persnickety...).

You may also be interested in these other projects if you're interested in taking more control of your phone and its privacy:

The /e/ project

Another alternate firmware but completely de-Google'd. They've taken vanilla open-source Android and patched it up to use non-Google substitutes for things like mapping, location services, etc, and/or built and hosted their own where there wasn't an existing one. It's a step beyond LineageOS in terms of de-Googling & securing your phone.

You can find most Google Play Store apps mirrored in their app store, so you don't have to miss out on much.

Far fewer phone models are supported than by Lineage. I've been experimenting with /e/ on my old Nexus 5. The only thing really stopping me is that that darned voice-activated assistant is actually really handy while driving or riding. You can retain the Google voice assistant in LineageOS; you cannot run it in /e/.

Purisim Librem 5

A radical departure from standard smartphone fare: open-source non-Android software, open-source (where possible) firmware, hardware killswitches & removable battery & storage.

They even have a model made entirely with parts sourced from the USA (for a pretty premium, though...).

They were kickstarted and just started shipping in late 2019, shipping rougher models to early adopters who were willing to trade that for getting one sooner. I did not back the project, but plan to order one of their final/finished production batch.
